rows.grounds: bodily winds or wind disorders as object
first member of compound naming the disease
second member and head of compound as object

items.question: Which specific winds and disease does the described practice claim to eliminate?
premises: The practice destroys the disease of leprosy.
The verb nāśayet is repeated for emphasis.
items.inference: The described practice is claimed to eliminate eighty wind disorders and the disease of leprosy.
uncertainties: Whether vātān refers to literal winds or specific bodily wind disorders is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: It destroys the eighty winds, and indeed destroys the disease of leprosy.
